title: Investigate timestamped deferred frees and KV shadow allocations causing steady GPU memory growth
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Production fleets exhibit gradual GPU memory growth during long-running continuous-batching workloads. Not a hard leak in user code — memory persists across many tens of thousands of requests and only drops after agent restart. Hypothesis: interplay between cudaMallocAsync deferred free timeline, stream reuse, and KV cache shadow allocations leaving arenas resident.
reproduction_steps: Run load generator against a model shard with sustained 100 qps and mixed prompt lengths (avg 1024 tokens) for 12+ hours in staging
Enable KV cache prefetching and continuous batching with config: batch_target=64, batch_timeout_ms=8
Monitor per-GPU resident set size and allocator slab stats using /metrics and nvprof snapshots every hour
Collect per-stream outstandingEventCount, lastFreeTimestamp, and cudaMemPool stats from runtime debug endpoints
observations: Resident GPU memory grows from ~12GB baseline to ~24GB over 10-14 hours on multi-tenant host
Allocator slab map shows multiple arenas with >90% resident pages but 'recent frees' timestamps that lag by 5-30 minutes
Heap snapshots indicate small 'shadow' allocations attributed to KV cache bookkeeping (~10-40MB each) created per-request and not released until stream event is recorded
Memory plateau only reduces after process restart or manual cudaMemPool trim (observed via a prototype admin API)
Symptoms are amplified when continuous-batching mixes low-latency and long-sequence requests on the same streams

experiments: Disable KV cache prefetching => growth rate reduced but not eliminated (12GB -> 16GB over same window)
Force stream fencing after each request (syncStream) => growth stops but tail latency increases ~20%
Set cudaMemPool trimming threshold to 64MB => immediate reduction after trim but gradual re-growth resumes
Per-stream allocator: switched to per-request transient pool (prototype) => eliminated shadow residency but increased peak allocation spikes
decision: Behavior appears to be a combinatorial issue: deferred frees from cudaMallocAsync are waiting on events that are delayed because streams are reused for continuous batching; KV cache bookkeeping creates short-lived allocations tied to those events which keep arenas resident. Short-term mitigation: add bounded async-fence when stream reuse crosses a configurable reuse count and trim mempool periodically. Long term: revise allocator's event-to-free policy so small metadata allocations can be freed eagerly or pooled in a non-GPU resident arena.
next_steps: Implement scoped stream-reuse counter + async fence: PR draft at https://github.com/redwood/re_runtime/pull/854 (Luca)
Add periodic cudaMemPool trimming background task behind feature flag (Aisha) — safe for Dedicated but opt-in for Hosted initially
Instrument per-stream outstanding event age metric and alert on >5m in Console; dashboard tile created: runtime -> allocator -> stale-event-age
Run 48h staging soak with flag enabled and collect memory slope regression compared to baseline
Follow-up RFC for allocator change: allow metadata frees to bypass device-resident arenas and go into host-resident pool (owner: Marcus, due 2025-03-18)
If mitigation stabilizes, schedule release in runtime-1.20 patch with flags: --stream-reuse-fence, --mempool-trim-interval
